title: Where Am I? (CD)
brief: In Windows CMD, running `cd` with no arguments prints the current directory. Run `cd` to see where you stand.
successMessage: In cmd.exe, `cd` alone displays the current drive and directory.

title: Directory Listing (DIR)
brief: Use `dir` to list files and subdirectories in the current folder.
successMessage: `dir` lists directory contents with creation dates, file sizes, and directory markers.

title: Show All Files (DIR /A)
brief: Windows hides a file with an attribute letter (H for Hidden) rather than a leading dot. Make `dir` show every file, hidden ones included.

hints.text: `dir` takes switches that start with a forward slash. The one for attributes is `/a`.

successMessage: `/a` displays files with specified attributes (hidden, system, archive).

title: Bare Listing (DIR /B)
brief: Produce a clean listing of this folder: names only, with no header, no sizes and no summary line. Use `dir`.

hints.text: The `dir` switch for a bare listing is `/b`.

successMessage: `dir /b` produces clean output ideal for batch processing and scripts.

title: Recursive Search (DIR /S)
brief: Search the `Documents` folder AND every folder inside it in one go. Use `dir`.

hints.text: The `dir` switch that recurses into subfolders is `/s`.

successMessage: `dir /s` walks subdirectories recursively.

title: Enter Documents (CD)
brief: Use `cd Documents` to move into the Documents directory.
successMessage: You changed your working directory to `C:\Users\Student\Documents`.

title: Climb to Parent (CD ..)
brief: Use `cd ..` from `Documents` to move back up to `C:\Users\Student`.
successMessage: `cd ..` navigates up to the parent directory.

title: Display File Content (TYPE)
brief: Print the contents of `Documents\notes.txt` to the prompt. Windows has no `cat`.

hints.text: The cmd.exe command that prints a file is `type`.

successMessage: `type` prints file contents to the screen (the Windows counterpart of `cat`).

title: Directory Tree (TREE)
brief: Display this directory and everything under it as a visual hierarchy rather than a flat list.

hints.text: The command is `tree`. Adding `/f` also lists the files.

successMessage: `tree` renders directory graphs. Add `/f` to include file names as well.

title: Locate Binaries (WHERE)
brief: Find out where on disk the Windows command interpreter itself lives — the file `cmd`.

hints.text: `where` searches the PATH for a named program, the way `which` does on Linux.

successMessage: `where` searches directories in PATH for matching executables.

title: Copy Files (COPY)
brief: Make a duplicate of `Documents\notes.txt` called `Documents\notes_backup.txt`.

hints.text: The cmd.exe command is `copy`. It takes the source path first, then the destination.

successMessage: `copy` creates duplicates of files.

title: Move Files (MOVE)
brief: Move `Desktop\todo.txt` into the `Documents` folder, keeping the same filename.

hints.text: The cmd.exe command is `move`. Source first, destination second.

successMessage: `move` relocates files to a new directory destination.

title: Rename Files (REN)
brief: Rename `Desktop\Shortcut.lnk` to `AppShortcut.lnk`. It must stay on the Desktop.

hints.text: The cmd.exe command is `ren`. Give it the existing path, then the NEW NAME only — not a second full path.

successMessage: `ren` (rename) changes file names.

title: Delete Files (DEL)
brief: Delete the file `Downloads\archive.zip`.

hints.text: The cmd.exe command is `del`. There is no Recycle Bin from the command prompt.

successMessage: `del` deletes files from disk.

title: Create Directories (MD / MKDIR)
brief: Create a new folder called `Projects` inside `C:\Users\Student`.

hints.text: cmd.exe accepts either `md` or the longer `mkdir`.

successMessage: `md` (Make Directory) creates folders in Windows.

title: Remove Directories (RD / RMDIR)
brief: Remove the `Projects` folder you just created.

hints.text: cmd.exe accepts either `rd` or the longer `rmdir`. The folder must be empty.

successMessage: `rd` (Remove Directory) deletes empty folders.

title: Inspect File Attributes (ATTRIB)
brief: `Documents\hidden_config.ini` does not appear in a plain `dir`. Show which attributes are set on it.

hints.text: `attrib` reports a file's attribute letters. H is Hidden, R is Read-only, S is System.

successMessage: `attrib` displays R (Read-only), H (Hidden), A (Archive), and S (System) attributes.

title: Environment Variables (%VAR%)
brief: cmd.exe wraps an environment variable in percent signs, like `%NAME%`. Print the value of your `USERPROFILE` variable.

hints.text: `echo` prints text, and the shell substitutes the variable before `echo` sees it.

successMessage: `%USERPROFILE%` expands to `C:\Users\Student`.

title: Setting Variables (SET)
brief: Create a new environment variable called `MY_VAR` and give it the value `123`.

hints.text: The cmd.exe command is `set`. Write the assignment with no spaces around the equals sign.

successMessage: `set` creates and manages environment variables in CMD.

title: Clear the Console (CLS)
brief: The screen is cluttered. Clear it.

hints.text: The cmd.exe command is `cls`, short for clear screen.

successMessage: `cls` clears the terminal screen in Windows CMD.

title: Pattern Search (FINDSTR)
brief: Show every line in `logs\eventlog.txt` that contains the phrase `EVENT ID`. Windows has no `grep`.

hints.text: The cmd.exe search command is `findstr`. Quote the phrase, because it contains a space.

successMessage: `findstr` is the Windows CMD counterpart of `grep`.

title: Case-Insensitive FINDSTR (/I)
brief: Find every mention of `defender` in `logs\eventlog.txt`, no matter how it is capitalised.

hints.text: `findstr` switches start with a forward slash. The one that ignores case is `/i`.

successMessage: `/i` specifies case-insensitive matching in `findstr`.

title: Count Lines (FIND /C /V "")
brief: Count how many lines `logs\firewall.log` contains. cmd.exe has no `wc`, so the standard trick is to print the file and pipe it into a counter that counts every line NOT matching an empty pattern.

hints.text: `type` prints the file, `|` pipes it onward, and `find` counts with `/c`. Add `/v ""` so it counts the lines that do not match nothing — that is, all of them.

successMessage: `find /c /v ""` counts every non-empty line — the standard Windows CMD equivalent of `wc -l`.

title: Process List (TASKLIST)
brief: Show every process running on this machine, with its memory use.

hints.text: The cmd.exe equivalent of Task Manager is a single command: `tasklist`.

successMessage: `tasklist` displays running applications and system services.

title: Network Configuration (IPCONFIG)
brief: Show this machine's IP address and network adapter configuration.

hints.text: The cmd.exe command is `ipconfig`. Adding `/all` shows much more detail.

successMessage: `ipconfig` displays TCP/IP network parameters.

title: System Information (SYSTEMINFO)
brief: Display the operating system build, installed memory and hardware summary for this machine.

hints.text: One command reports the whole system summary: `systeminfo`.

successMessage: `systeminfo` outputs full system diagnostic metrics.

title: Cryptographic Hash (CERTUTIL)
brief: Compute the MD5 checksum of `Documents\data.csv` for a chain-of-custody record. Windows has no `md5sum`; the built-in tool is `certutil`.

hints.text: `certutil` needs the `-hashfile` switch, then the file path, then the algorithm name in capitals.

successMessage: Congratulations! You have completed Windows CMD Essentials and mastered the Windows command-line toolset.
